I.}}</noinclude>they liked not to haue God in knovvledge: God deliuered them vp into a reprobate sense: to doe those things that are not conuenient: {{verse|chapter=1|verse=29}}† replenished vvith al iniquitie, malice, fornication, auarice, vvickednes, ful of enuie, murder, contention, guile, malignitie, vvhisperers, {{verse|chapter=1|verse=30}}† detractours, odible to God, contumelious, proude, hautie, inuentours of euil things, disobedient to parents, {{verse|chapter=1|verse=31}}† folish, dissolute, vvithout affection, vvithout fidelitie, vvithout mercie. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=32}}† Who vvhereas they knevv the iustice of God, did not vnderstand that they vvhich doe such things, are {{sup|‖}} vvorthie of death: not only they that doe them, but they also that consent to the doers.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. I.}}}}

''7. Grace to you and peace.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Apostolical salutation or blessing.}}It is a kind of blessing rather then a prophane salutation, proper to the Apostles, of greater vertue then the benedictions of the fathers in the old Testament. The holy fathers of the Church seemed to absteine from it for their reuerence to the Apostles. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Epiph. hæres. 66.''}}The Manichees ''(August. cont. ep. funda. c. 5. 6''.) and other Heretikes {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The same vsed of Heretikes.}}(as also these of our time) because they vvould be counted Apostles, often vse it.

''8. Your faith renoumed.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Romane faith highly commended.}}The holy Doctors vpon these wordes of the Apostle, and specially by our Masters promise {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 22.''}}made to Peter, that his faith should not faile, giue great testimonie for the prouidence of God in the preseruation of the Romane faith. S. Cyprian thus: ep. 55. nu. 6. ''They are so bold to cary letters from prophane Schismatikes to the chaire of Peter and the principal Church whence Priestly vnitie rose: not considering the Romanes to be them whose faith (the Apostle being the commender) was praised, to whom misbelief cannot haue accesse.'' So S. Hierom Apolog. adu. Ruff. li. 3. c. 4. to. 2. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=It can not faile, nor be corrupted.}}''know you, that the Romane faith commended by the Apostles mouth, wil receiue no such deceites, nor can be possibly changed, though an Angel taught othervvise, being fensed by S. Paules authoritie.'' Againe ep. 63. ad Pammach. & Oceanum. c. 4. to. 2. ''Whatsoeuer thou be that auouchest new sectes, I pray thee haue respect to the Romane eares. Spare the faith which was praised by the Apostles voice.'' And in another place{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Prooem. li. 2. Com. in ep. ad Gal''.}}: ''Will ye know, o Paula and Eustochium, hovv the Apostle hath noted euery prouince vvith their proprieties? The faith of the people of Rome is praised. Where is there so great concourse to Churches and Martyrs' sepulchres?'' {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Romane stations, a token of greater faith and deuotion.}}''Where soundeth Amen like thunder from heauen, or where are the temples (void of Idols) so shaken as there? Not that the Romanes haue another faith then the rest of the Christian Churches, but that there is in them more deuotion and simplicitie of faith.'' In another place the same holy Doctor signifieth that it is al one to say, the Romane faith, and the Catholike. ''Apolog. 1. adu. Ruff. c. 1.'' So doth S. Cyprian ''ep. 52. num. 1. ad Antonianum'': and S. Ambrose ''de obitu fratris, in med.'' {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Catholike and Romane faith al one.}}Whereupon, this vvord, ''Roman'', is added to, ''Catholic'', in many countries where Sectes do abound, for the better distinction of true beleeuers from Heretikes: which in al ages did hate and abhorre the Romane faith and Church, as al malefactors do their Iudges and correctors.

''9. Serue in spirit.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=How God is serued in spirit.}}Diuerse Heretikes when they heare that God is a spirit, and must be serued and adored in spirit, imagine, that he must be honoured only invvardly, vvithout ceremonies and external workes: vvhich you see is othervvise, for that the Apostle serued God in spirit, by preaching the Gospel. To serue God then in spirit, is to serue him with faith, hope, and charitie, and vvith al workes proceding of them: as to serue him carnally, is, vvith vvorkes external, vvithout the said internal vertues.

''9. A memorie of you.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Praier for conuersion of soules.}}A great example of charitie for al men, specially for Prelates and Pastors, not only to preach, but to pray continually for the conuersion of people to Christes faith: vvhich the Apostle did for them vvhom he neuer knew, in respect of Gods honour only and the zeale of soules.

''15. To euangelize.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel is not only the Written Word.}}The Gospel is not only the life of our Sauiour written by the foure Euangelistes, nor only that vvhich is written in the nevv Testament: but their vvhole course of preaching and teaching the faith. Vvhich faith commeth ordinarily of preaching and hearing, and not of writing or reading. And therfore S. Paul thought not him self discharged by writing to the Romanes, but his desire vvas to preach vnto them: for that was the proper commission giuen to the<noinclude>{{rh|||Apostles,}}</noinclude>
